title.orig: PEP 8 – Style Guide for Python Code (Introduction; A Foolish Consistency is the Hobgoblin of Little Minds)

author.orig: Guido van Rossum, Barry Warsaw, Alyssa Coghlan

author.zh: 吉多·范罗苏姆、巴里·华沙、艾丽莎·科格伦

edition.en: The first two sections of PEP 8 as published on peps.python.org; a footnote marker is omitted.
edition.zh: 据 peps.python.org 所载 PEP 8 的前两节；一处脚注标记从略。

note.en: PEP 8 is the style guide for Python's standard library, and much of the world's Python follows it; these are its opening sections, before the rules about spaces and line lengths. The second section's title borrows Emerson's line about foolish consistency. Notice where it puts the weight: code is read much more often than it is written, and a guideline that makes code harder to read should be set aside.
note.zh: PEP 8 是 Python 标准库的风格指南，世界上大量 Python 代码都遵循它；这里是它的开头两节，在那些关于空格和行长的规则之前。第二节的标题借用了爱默生关于“愚蠢的一致性”的名句。请留意它把重心放在哪里：代码被阅读的次数远多于被编写的次数，一条让代码更难读的准则就应当放下。

excerpt.orig: One of Guido’s key insights is that code is read much more often than it is written.
excerpt.en: One of Guido’s key insights is that code is read much more often than it is written.
excerpt.zh: Guido 的一个关键洞见是：代码被阅读的次数远多于被编写的次数。
